name: OS Exhaustion Flood
summary: Adversaries may launch a denial of service (DoS) attack targeting an endpoint's operating system (OS). A system's OS is responsible for managing the finite resources as well as preventing the entire system from being overwhelmed by excessive demands on its capacity. These attacks do not need to exhaust the actual resources on a system; the attacks may simply exhaust the limits and available resources that an OS self-imposes. Different ways to…

strategies.name: Endpoint DoS via OS Exhaustion Flood Detection Strategy

analytics.name: Analytic 1012
analytics.guidance: Burst of incomplete TCP handshakes (e.g., SYN floods) or uncorrelated ACK packets targeting the state table resulting in OS resource exhaustion.

analytics.name: Analytic 1013
analytics.guidance: Flood of spoofed SYN or ACK packets causing exhaustion of OS TCP state table, potentially via user-space utilities or kernel-level DoS agents.

analytics.name: Analytic 1014
analytics.guidance: Adversary tool/script issuing mass SYN/ACK floods that degrade OS responsiveness and interrupt service response on macOS endpoints.
